title: DKA Lab Correction Over Time
scenario: A 24-year-old client with type 1 diabetes is admitted for diabetic ketoacidosis and started on an IV insulin infusion with fluid and electrolyte replacement. Serial labs are drawn over the first eight hours of treatment.

questions.subject: Medical-Surgical
questions.stem: Reviewing the serial laboratory trend, which findings indicate that the diabetic ketoacidosis is resolving? Select all that apply.

options.text: Potassium is rising above the reference range
Glucose has returned to the normal range

questions.rationale: Resolution of DKA is shown by falling glucose, a rising pH and bicarbonate, and a closing anion gap. Potassium is falling (not rising) as insulin drives it intracellularly, and glucose remains elevated at 8 hours.

questions.subject: Medical-Surgical
questions.stem: Based on the 8-hour potassium trend, which action should the nurse anticipate?

options.text: Add potassium to the IV fluids per protocol
Administer a rapid IV insulin bolus

questions.rationale: Insulin drives potassium into cells, and the trend shows potassium falling toward the low-normal range (3.4 mEq/L); protocols call for adding potassium to IV fluids to prevent hypokalemia while the insulin infusion continues.
